newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Diesel well offered as prices dip.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Diesel well offered as prices dip.

text.p: Singapore gas oil market was well offered on Monday with as many as eight sellers offering at least 10 cargoes, as prices continued to slip, traders said.
"The market is still fundamentally weak," one trader said. "People are anxious with the abundant supplies which are in storage tanks."
Traders also noted that the weakness is seen in the MidEast as well, which is expected to last for at least two more months.
A U.S. major sold to a Japanese trader 150,000-barrel at $24.80 per barrel fob for June 10-14, 10 cent below Friday's traded level.
Other offers were seen at $24.90-$25.00 with bids at $24.70-$24.80.
But June swaps were steady at Friday's level of $24.85/$24.95 with a trade seen at $24.90.
Jet fuel remained under pressure, with offers around last week's deal of $24.40.

But traders said slight support is expected from Sri Lanka, which is expected to buy additional volumes of gas oil and jet fuel for June over and above the amount that they have tendered for June 10-11 delivery.
The additional volume which would be decided on Tuesday is due to the unscheduled shutdown of its 55,000-barrel-per-day refinery for one week during the first week of June.

Bangladesh's import tender for July-December deliveries received aggressive offers from Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC) and Malaysia's Petco, traders said. KPC offered gas oil under Group B which seeks 3.335 million barrels at $1.30 per barrel above Singapore quotes cost-and-freight Chittagong.
Petco's offer under Group A for gas oil, kerosene and jet fuel was at a $1.60-premium, c-and-f.
